title: Threat intelligence: which warnings deserve your time, and what do you do with them?
short: Subscribe to CERT-Bund, the KEV catalogs and your vendors' advisories, and give every warning that matches your inventory an owner and a decision within one working day, the same day if it is exploited and exposed.
answer: This month, write down the products, suppliers and sector you need warnings about, and subscribe to the free sources that cover them: CERT-Bund's WID, CISA's and ENISA's catalogs of exploited vulnerabilities and your vendors' advisories. Give every warning that matches your inventory an owner and a decision (patch, block, hunt or detect) within one working day, or the same day if it is exploited and exposed, and judge your intelligence by the actions it produced, not by what you read.
audience: IT and security teams in EU organizations of any size, many in Germany, from teams without analysts to those with a small SOC

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Write down what you need to know.
items.text: List your internet-facing products and versions, critical suppliers, sector and countries. A warning that touches none of them is reading, not work.

items.title: Subscribe to the free primary sources.
items.text: Follow CERT-Bund's WID, which publishes short advisories for organizations on its portal and by RSS[^wid]. Add CISA KEV[^kev], ENISA's EU KEV[^enisavs] and your vendors' advisories.

items.title: Filter by your inventory, then act on every match.
items.text: WID lists 4,250 advisories first published in 2026 by 5 November, 55% more than in all of 2025[^widcsaf]. CISA added 284 to KEV in the same period[^kev]: few enough to check each one.

items.title: Detect techniques, not just indicators.
items.text: The NCSC warns that indicators from China-linked covert networks "disappear as quickly as they are discovered"[^ncsccovert]. Build lasting detections on the behavior an advisory describes[^mtrends].

items.title: Join one sharing community.
items.text: In Germany, the Allianz für Cyber-Sicherheit is free for organizations with a seat or branch there[^acs] and passes on the BSI's confidential TLP-labeled warnings[^csw]. Elsewhere, ask your national CERT or your sector's ISAC.

blocks.title: Turn a warning into an action

items.title: Does it touch something on your list?
items.text: Match product, version and exposure against the inventory. CSAF, the JSON format of CERT-Bund's feed[^widcsaf], lets tools compare advisories with an asset database or SBOM[^csaf].

items.title: Is it being exploited?
items.text: Check KEV, EU KEV and the advisory. Verizon found the chance of renewed exploitation roughly halves 30 days after the last observed activity[^dbir], so when you must choose, put recent activity first.

items.title: Which action fits?
items.text: Patch or contain within the patching sheet's deadlines. Block indicators that are recent and specific. Hunt in your logs back to the first known exploitation. Add a detection when the advisory describes a technique your logs can show.

items.title: Who does it, and did it hold?
items.text: Open a ticket with one owner and a due date. Close it with the outcome (patched, blocked, nothing found or not affected) once a check confirms it.

blocks.title: Decide what you need to know
items: **Your technology.** Edge devices, identity, remote access and what suppliers run for you. ENISA knew the vector of only 5.2% of unauthorized access incidents in the EU in 2025; 60.4% of those used a vulnerability[^etl].

**Your sector and region.** Public administration, business services, transport, manufacturing and finance were the most affected EU sectors in 2025, and ideology-driven operations made up 57.3% of incidents[^etl].
**Your suppliers and your own alerts.** Add your MSP and cloud suppliers, and feed phishing reports and blocked sign-ins back in.

**Strategic reports, once a year.** Read your sector's part of the ENISA Threat Landscape[^etl], the BSI's Lagebericht[^bsilage] and M-Trends or the DBIR. Take one or two changes in priority from each.

blocks.title: Free sources worth subscribing to
items: **CERT-Bund's WID.** Short advisories for organizations on the portal and by RSS[^wid], and a CSAF feed for automated matching[^widcsaf].
**CISA KEV and ENISA's EU KEV.** KEV lists 1,768 exploited vulnerabilities[^kev], EU KEV those confirmed exploited against EU entities[^enisavs].
**Vendor advisories** for every product on your list. NIS2's rules for digital providers name suppliers as a channel to monitor[^nis2ir].
**The BSI-Portal and the ACS.** Participants get BSI security notices (BITS), warnings and daily and monthly situation reports[^acsportal].
**Microsoft Defender threat analytics.** Reports show exposed devices and recommended actions, with any Defender license except Endpoint P1[^msta].
**Exposure alerts** about your own addresses: see the attack surface sheet.

blocks.title: Indicators, techniques and ATT&CK
items: **Indicators expire.** Hashes, IP addresses and domains are the easiest things for an attacker to change; techniques are the costliest[^pop]. Give each blocked indicator an expiry date, such as 30 days for IP addresses.
**Search the past.** When an advisory lists indicators, search your logs back to the campaign's start. A hit means incident response, not just a block.
**Build lasting detections on behavior.** Mandiant advises it because attackers rapidly change infrastructure and run malware in memory[^mtrends].
**Tag rules with ATT&CK technique IDs.** Start from the detection strategies MITRE has linked to techniques since v18[^attack18], but don't chase 100% coverage[^attres].

blocks.title: Share what you see
items: **EU law encourages it.** NIS2 Article 29 has member states let entities share indicators, TTPs and alerts voluntarily in sharing arrangements, including with suppliers[^nis2]. DORA Article 45 covers financial entities[^dora].
**Personal data needs a basis.** NIS2 recital 121 says legitimate interest under GDPR Article 6(1)(f) could cover sharing IP addresses and URLs[^nis2].
**Check whether to tell the authority.** DORA requires it[^dora], and NIS2 asks member states to require it[^nis2]. Under BSIG § 30(7), sharing on the BSI's platform adds no obligations[^bsig].
**Label with TLP 2.0.** CLEAR is public, GREEN stays in the community, AMBER in your organization and its clients, AMBER+STRICT in your organization, RED only with the individual recipients[^tlp].

blocks.title: Is it changing anything?
items: **Actions per month.** Patches, blocks, hunts and detections that started from a warning. Review any source that produced none for two quarters.
**Time from advisory to decision.** For warnings that match your list. Aim for one working day, the same day if exploited and exposed.
**Learned too late.** Exploited flaws in your products you first heard about from a customer, supplier or the news.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **The ACS moved into the BSI-Portal in January 2026.** Existing participants must re-register there, with an ELSTER company login, by 31 January 2027 or lose their participation[^acsportal].
**ATT&CK v19 split Defense Evasion** into Stealth and Defense Impairment in April[^attack19]. Re-tag your rules. v20 added AI techniques in October[^attack20].
**EU KEV will add manufacturers' reports.** The CRA has required them since 11 September 2026[^enisavs].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Paid feeds before free ones turn into tickets.** Only 26% of KEV vulnerabilities in Verizon's data were fully fixed in 2025, and full fixes took a median of 43 days[^dbir].
**Indicator lists without context.** Without campaign, date and confidence you can't judge them, and IP lists go stale fast[^ncsccovert].
**Tracking actor names.** Microsoft lists 12 other names for its Forest Blizzard, APT28 among them[^msnames]. Track techniques instead.
**A threat intelligence platform before a process.** A mailbox, a ticket queue and a one-page requirements list come first.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Reading without a ticket.** A warning that ends in a chat has no owner. Every match gets a ticket, even when the answer is "not affected".
**Blocking feeds unfiltered.** Feeds can include public DNS resolvers, popular domains and scanners. Check them against MISP's warninglists[^mispwl].
**Forwarding labeled warnings to suppliers.** TLP:AMBER covers your organization and its clients, not your MSP. Ask the source first[^tlp].
**Stale filters.** Update feed filters and subscriptions when you add a product. NIS2's rules for digital providers require reviewing these channels at planned intervals[^nis2ir].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Send WID's RSS feed and your vendors' advisories, filtered to your internet-facing products, to a mailbox two people read.
Join the ACS, or your national CERT's community.
Ask your IT provider which advisories it acted on last month.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Pull KEV, EU KEV and vendor CSAF feeds into tickets, matched against the inventory.
Add one detection a month from an advisory relevant to your sector.
Run MISP, which is free and open source[^misp], or use your ISAC's.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Review intelligence requirements with risk owners every quarter.
Keep a register of the sharing arrangements you join and the notifications you made.
Put TLP handling in your MSSP contract and report the three measures to leadership.

changes.text: Published after a copy edit and a source-by-source fact check, which recomputed every count and narrowed 12 statements to what the sources say.
First draft, based on NIS2, DORA, the BSIG, TLP 2.0, the CERT-Bund, CISA and ENISA feeds, ATT&CK and the 2026 reports from ENISA, Mandiant and Verizon.
